Nothing is missing and every customer ID is unique.
A few codes are not in the official description (for example education codes 0, 5 and 6). They were kept as their own groups, not deleted.
Negative bill amounts mean the customer had paid more than they owed (a credit balance). That is normal.

summary: We looked at 30,120 credit-card customers. 6,673 of them (about 1 in 5) missed their payment the following month.
The model sorted every customer into a risk group: 24,364 low, 2,235 medium and 3,521 high risk.
The clearest warning sign is paying late recently: customers who were 2 or more months late in September missed their next payment 69% of the time, compared with 17% for everyone else.
These are estimates based on past behaviour. They show who is more likely to miss a payment, not who certainly will.
